purpose: HD-11 regression fixture (the second, alongside GX-19): a strictly monotonic decline contains ZERO k=3 pivot highs, yet the all-highs upper-log-hull still yields a canonical second anchor — the hull binds at the FIRST later bar, B*=(1,98), giving an ACTIVE line. A pivot-restricted prefilter would find no candidate at all and wrongly emit NO_VALID_SECOND_ANCHOR; under §6/§8 candidacy is over every later bar high, so a monotonic decline can never emit that code.
category: normal valid (monotonic decline) — HD-11 regression: zero-pivot series with a canonical anchor

params.eps_break_note: eps_break is illustrative, not locked (HD-03, §13.5). No breakout occurs in this fixture, so eps_break is not exercised. Envelope domination is governed by params.eps=0.02 only (§9) — eps_touch and eps_break never govern it.

expected_second_anchor.reason: All-highs upper-log-hull vertex: the shallowest descending line from A that dominates every later bar high within eps. With H[t]=100-2t the candidate slope is m(t)=ln(1-0.02t)/t, which is strictly decreasing in t, so the shallowest slope is at t=1. NOT a k=3 pivot — the series contains no pivot high at all (isPivotHigh needs H[p] > H[p-1], never true here) — yet canonical per §6/§8, D-TL-03/D-TL-05 and HD-11.

rejection_rationale.candidate: NO_VALID_SECOND_ANCHOR — the outcome this fixture previously expected, on the ground that no k=3 pivot high exists
rejection_rationale.rejected_because: Pivot status is NOT a precondition for second-anchor candidacy (§6: 'There is no isPivotHigh(tB,k) precondition'; §5 and D-TL-03: pivots are secondary/non-authoritative; HD-11). Candidacy is over EVERY later bar high with HB < HA, so the absence of k-pivots cannot by itself produce this reason code. A fixture may not return NO_VALID_SECOND_ANCHOR merely because no k-pivot exists; the code fires only when NO candidate survives the §8 envelope test (the genuinely reachable case is GX-20, a duplicate ATH).
rejection_rationale.numeric: k=3 pivots in this series: ZERO (isPivotHigh(p,3) requires H[p] > H[p-1]; H is strictly decreasing, so the strict-left test fails at every p>=1). Eligible candidates per §6: t=1..14 -> 14 candidates. Envelope-valid at eps=0.02: 14 of 14. Envelope-valid at eps=0: exactly 1 (t=1). Selected B* = (1,98).

rejection_rationale.candidate: B=(2,96) — the next bar; what a 'shallowest line that stays strictly above every high' reading would prefer
rejection_rationale.rejected_because: Among envelope-valid candidates §8 step 4 selects the SHALLOWEST descending line (slope closest to zero). m(2) is steeper than m(1), so (2,96) is not the hull vertex. Its line also passes marginally BELOW the t=1 high; it is envelope-valid only because that shortfall (0.000208) sits inside eps=0.02.

rejection_rationale.candidate: B=(14,72) — the last and lowest bar (a naive 'most recent low' / steepest-line choice)
rejection_rationale.rejected_because: It is envelope-valid at eps=0.02 but far from the hull vertex: its line is the steepest of the 14 candidates and dips up to 0.0134 log units below the intervening highs. §8 selects the shallowest dominating line, not the steepest.

rejection_rationale.candidate: INSUFFICIENT_BARS or ATH_TOO_RECENT instead of a line
rejection_rationale.rejected_because: Neither guard fires: the series is long enough and the ATH is the FIRST of 15 bars, leaving 14 later bars for the descent (§18).
rejection_rationale.numeric: INSUFFICIENT_BARS needs n < 2k+2 = 8; n = 15 -> does not fire. ATH_TOO_RECENT needs the ATH on or within k=3 of the LAST bar; tA=0 with 14 later bars -> does not fire. All prices > 0 and max |y[t]-y[t-1]| = ln(74/72) = 0.0273999 << ln(1.5) = 0.405465 -> no INVALID_PRICE, no SUSPECTED_UNADJUSTED_SPLIT.

rejection_rationale.rejected_because: No bar high and no daily close ever exceeds the line (let alone line + eps_break), because line(t)=100*0.98^t >= 100-2t = H[t] for every t (Bernoulli's inequality) and C[t] <= H[t]. End state is ACTIVE with breakout_bar = confirmed_bar = null and no retest.
rejection_rationale.numeric: Tightest close: t=2, ln(C[2])=ln96=4.564348 vs y_hat(2)+eps_break=4.564765+0.01=4.574765 -> misses by 0.010417. Tightest high: t=1, ln98=4.584967 = y_hat(1) exactly (B* lies on the line). No t satisfies ln(C[t]) > y_hat(t)+eps_break or ln(H[t]) > y_hat(t)+eps.

key_inequalities: Anchor A=(0,100): earliest bar at the global max, unique (§4, D-TL-02). yA=ln100=4.605170.
Candidate set = ALL later bar highs with HB < HA (§6): t=1..14 -> 14 candidates. There is NO isPivotHigh(tB,k) precondition (§6, §5, D-TL-03, HD-11); the series in fact contains ZERO k=3 pivots.

Highs are H[t]=100-2t, so slope(A->t)=ln(1-0.02t)/t. ln(1-0.02t) is concave with value 0 at t=0, hence ln(1-0.02t)/t is strictly DECREASING in t: m(1)=-0.0202027 > m(2)=-0.0204110 > m(7)=-0.0215461 > m(14)=-0.0234646. The shallowest (hull) candidate is therefore t=1.

Domination over EVERY bar high (§8 step 3, D-TL-05): gap(t)=y[t]-y_hat(t)=ln(1-0.02t)+0.0202027073*t <= 0 for all t, so B* has 0 violations even at eps=0. Worst (largest) gap among t>=2 is at t=2: ln(0.96)+0.0404054=-0.0408220+0.0404054=-0.00041658.

Envelope tolerance is params.eps=0.02 (§9) — distinct from eps_touch=0.01 and eps_break=0.01, neither of which governs domination. At eps=0.02 ALL 14/14 candidates are envelope-valid (the worst case, t=14, peaks at +0.013429 < 0.02). At eps=0 exactly ONE survives: B* itself, because any candidate t0>=2 satisfies (1-0.02*t0)^(1/t0) < 0.98, so its line lies below 98 at t=1 and the t=1 high pierces it.
Selection (§8 step 4) among envelope-valid candidates = argmax slope = t=1 -> B*=(1,98), m=-0.0202027, b=4.605170. No ENVELOPE_TIE_LATER (all 14 slopes are distinct).
Touches (eps_touch=0.01, §12): |gap(t)| <= 0.01 for t=0..7 (t=7: 0.0094039) and > eps_touch from t=8 (0.0127317). A and B* are touches 1 and 2.
Guards silent: n=15 >= 2k+2=8 (no INSUFFICIENT_BARS); tA=0 with 14 later bars (no ATH_TOO_RECENT); all prices > 0; max |y[t]-y[t-1]|=ln(74/72)=0.0273999 << ln1.5=0.405465.

State: no close exceeds line+eps_break anywhere (line(t)=100*0.98^t >= 100-2t = C[t] for t>=1; C[0]=99 < 100) -> LINE_ESTABLISHED at t=1, final state ACTIVE, breakout_bar=null, confirmed_bar=null, no retest.

HD-11 regression: a k=3 pivot PREFILTER finds ZERO candidates here and would wrongly emit NO_VALID_SECOND_ANCHOR, while the all-highs hull yields B*=(1,98). Under §6, a strictly monotonic decline ALWAYS has an eligible B (the first later bar high), so it can NEVER produce NO_VALID_SECOND_ANCHOR.

pivot_analysis.selected_anchor_local_high_order: none — H[1]=98 < H[0]=100, so t=1 fails the strict-left test at every order k>=1; no bar in the series is a pivot high
pivot_analysis.note: Complements GX-19: there the canonical anchor is a non-pivot bar in a series that HAS a pivot; here the series has NO pivots at all and the canonical anchor still exists. Pivot status is non-authoritative for selection (§5, D-TL-03, D-TL-05, HD-11).

geometry_check.notes: Small, hand-verifiable (15 bars, highs 100,98,96,...,72). Geometry to 6 significant figures; where hand exp() is ambiguous at the 6th figure the inequalities above (not the rounded line display) are authoritative, per fixtures/README.md §2. CORRECTED under Issue #16 (2026-07-25): the previously committed expected output asserted NO_VALID_SECOND_ANCHOR on the pivot-high precondition that HD-11 removed. This correction re-derives the fixture against the already-approved all-highs rule (§5/§6/§8, D-TL-03/D-TL-05); it changes NO rule.
